speaker: Doctor
text: Let me start by understanding the nature of your skin concern. Can you describe the appearance, color, and size of the lesion(s) you are worried about? Have you noticed any changes in their shape, border, or symptoms such as bleeding or itching?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the detailed history; the non-healing nature of these lesions on your penis and finger, combined with your smoking history and failed prior treatments, raises significant concern for malignancy. Are you currently experiencing pain, ulceration, or discharge from either lesion, and how long have they been present?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC), Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, and HIV serology.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Non-healing, crusty, red lesions on the penile shaft and left middle finger. I also have Lesions are painless, History of unsuccessful treatment for syphilis and eczema. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (penile and acral).
